  unchanged:** pages with text are still skipped.
- **Dialog (`crates/ui-egui/src/ocr_ui.rs`):** a new "Also recognize pages that already have text"

title: Issue #1185: Protect refuses passwords that encryption would make empty or equal
author: jay-tau
body:
Fixes #1185.

New encryption doesn't key on a password as typed:
- **AES-256.** `sasl_password` applies SASLprep (ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4.3.3, RFC 4013), falls back to the password as given if SASLprep refuses it, and truncates the UTF-8 to 127 bytes.
- **R2–R4.** Passwords are encoded in PDFDocEncoding, then cut or padded to exactly 32 bytes (the padding starts with `(`).

`Protection::validate` checked only the typed strings, so Protect accepted passwords that come out as the empty password, or as the other password. A permissions password of `"\u{AD}"` lets anyone open the file as owner. Open `"A"` with permissions `"\u{FF21}"`, or RC4/AES-128 open `"a"`×31 with permissions `"a"`×31 + `"("`, lets the open password lift the restrictions. #1185 has the full table.

## What changes
- **crypt.** New `effective_password(algorithm, password)` returns the bytes the keys are derived from: the prepared password, padded to 32 bytes for R2–R4. `create` now prepares both passwords through the same private helper it is built on. It is re-exported from `pdfcraft-cos`, as `Algorithm` already is. What `create` writes and how files open are unchanged, including the R2–R4 rule that an empty owner password means the user password.
- **engine.** `Protection::validate` keeps its checks and adds two:
  - a password whose effective bytes are those of `""` is refused with "passwords can't be empty or made only of characters that passwords ignore, such as soft hyphens";
  - an open and a permissions password with equal effective bytes are refused with "the open password and the permissions password must be different (PDF readers treat these two as the same password)".
- **UI.** No UI code or translation entries change. Apply in the Protect dialog shows the engine's (English) message in the existing "Protect with password failed: …" toast (`editing.rs`). `ProtectDraft::problem()` doesn't pre-check these cases.

## Unchanged
- Opening documents. Tests confirm that `"A"` with `"\u{FF21}\u{FF22}"…

title: Raise workspace rust-version to 1.95 to match the UI crate (#1169)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1169.

The root `Cargo.toml` said `rust-version = "1.90"`, but `crates/ui-egui` declares 1.95 and its dependencies (`egui`/`eframe` 0.36.2, `craft-ui`) need 1.95 too. A build with an older toolchain failed with "rustc 1.93.0 is not supported" instead of the workspace stating the real minimum.

- `Cargo.toml`: workspace `rust-version` is now `1.95`, the same as `crates/ui-egui/Cargo.toml`.
- `README.md`: the "Get started" section now says that building needs Rust 1.95 or later, as the issue suggested.
- `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/development.md`: the version they give changes from 1.90 to 1.95. `docs/development.md` no longer says that the core-crate minimum is lower.
- `xtask/src/version.rs`: new test `workspace_rust_version_covers_the_ui_crate`. It reads both manifests and checks that the workspace minimum is not lower than the UI crate's minimum. It fails on `main` (1.90 < 1.95) and passes with this change, so the two cannot drift apart again without a failing test.

CI uses stable, so nothing changes there.

title: Web: preserve PDF sessions and deduplicate clipboard gestures
author: mmmbeer
body:
Browser page shortcuts and organizer actions could independently consume the same clipboard gesture. This ports the existing *craft command-layer Copy/Cut/Paste routing and cross-frame gesture matching while preserving focused text and form controls. Pages keep their internal clipboard semantics.

Browser checkpoints restore ordered PDF tabs, active document, PDF snapshots and both history stacks, dirty status, per-document current page, scroll offset, zoom, fit, page layout, continuous-page mode, rotation and navigation history. The port preserves upstream's newer page-layout and camera actions, and localizable history labels with dynamic document values.

Addresses the browser session-restoration portion of #418 and #1178. Desktop persistence and independently reopening a document after explicitly closing it are not implemented here, so neither report is automatically closed.

Validation: nine standalone storage tests passed for this app at the root URL; the common harness extracting the actual production clipboard routers/PNG decoder passed eight tests. All four applications passed local WebAssembly checks and native engine session/history round-trip tests. No GitHub Actions build was requested.

This is a draft port of existing code onto upstream main as captured by the fork. Launcher, shared fonts, branding removals and hosting changes are excluded. See docs/browser-session-recovery.md for storage limits, migration and testing details. The JavaScript IndexedDB/lifecycle coordinator is an explicit architecture proposal for review against the Rust-only repository preference.

Pending before merge: repository-wide quality checks and real Chromium/Firefox/WebKit clipboard permission, menu/keyboard, text focus, stale destination, refresh/return, duplicated-tab and large-history review. Compilation and fake-DOM storage tests do not establish complete browser behavior. AI assistance was used to port and review the changes.

title: Release workflow: pass the Azure signing secrets
author: echelon
body:
Since this repo's `release.yml` moved to `storytold/craft-common-actions`, it has passed the Apple and `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE*` secrets to the shared workflow, but not the six `AZURE_*` secrets that Azure Trusted Signing uses.

The shared workflow's signing jobs run in this repo's `release` environment and read the values from there, but only for names the caller lists. So the next release would have built **unsigned** Windows MSIs and portable zips, with only a warning. craft-launcher 0.3.1 did exactly this, and storytold/craft-launcher#174 fixed it with this same change.

This adds the six names. All twelve secrets are already set in this repo's `release` environment. storytold/craft-common-actions#3 makes release builds fail outright if signing secrets are missing, and fixes the riscv64 `--formats` call. This PR should land first.

`actionlint` passes.
